title: Reject a cross-tenant cache read before lookup
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed lib/tenant-report.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
const reports=new Map();
export async function report(id:string){if(!reports.has(id))reports.set(id,await queryReport(id));return reports.get(id);}

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Request the same local ID in two tenants.
Attempt a forged tenant parameter and a revoked membership.
Inspect all serialized props and HTTP caches for leaked representations.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: A resource ID by itself may not identify an authorized representation.
Request the same local ID in two tenants.
alternativeApproaches: Only if the output is identical for every authorized role. Otherwise include the relevant representation version/scope or avoid shared caching. Authorization must still run before access, with a defined revocation freshness policy.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
